patterns: something seems to have gone awry
cause a plan to go awry

usage.predicative: Awry most commonly follows go: The plan went awry.
usage.attributive: It is not normally placed directly before a noun; use a failed plan rather than an awry plan.
usage.adverbial: Its older physical sense can function adverbially, meaning crookedly or in the wrong direction.
usage.comparison: Comparative and superlative forms are generally avoided.
usage.pronunciation: The stress falls on the second syllable, and awry rhymes with a cry, not with sorry.

ja: 計画・試み・状況などが予想どおりに進まず、失敗して
物事の進行が正しい方向から外れて、おかしくなって
期待・意図した結果とは異なる状態になって
物理的に曲がって、斜めになって、位置がずれて
古風な用法で、疑い・非難などを含む横目で
en: for a plan, attempt, or situation, unsuccessfully or contrary to expectation
off the proper course or developing in a problematic way
producing a result different from what was intended
physically crooked, tilted, or displaced from the correct position
in an older use, with a suspicious, disapproving, or sidelong look

nuance.ja: 現代英語の awry は主として go awry の形で使われ、慎重に立てた計画や正常に進んでいた手続きが、何らかの問題によって意図した方向から外れることを表す。単なる失敗だけでなく、「途中で何かがおかしくなった」という過程を感じさせる。Something went wrong. より少し文語的で、物語・報道・ビジネス上の説明にも使われる。if anything goes awry は「万一何か問題が生じたら」という意味になる。物理的な「斜めに、ねじれて」という意味は現代では比較的まれで、askew や crooked の方が一般的である。
nuance.en: In modern English, awry occurs chiefly in go awry and describes a planned or initially orderly process departing from its intended course because something has gone wrong. It suggests not only failure but a development that became defective along the way. It is slightly more literary than something went wrong and is common in narrative, journalism, and business accounts. If anything goes awry means if any unexpected problem occurs. The physical sense crookedly or at an angle is now less common, and askew or crooked is generally more natural.

ja: awry：計画・状況が意図した方向から外れ、うまくいかなくなって。
wrong：誤って、不具合が生じて、期待と異なって。最も一般的。
amiss：何かがおかしい、正常でない。原因不明の違和感にも使う。
off track：計画・議論・進行が本来の方向からそれて。
askew：物が斜め・不均衡な位置にある。物理的配置に多い。
crooked：直線でなく曲がった、または不正直な。
backfire：計画・行動が意図と逆の悪い結果をもたらす。
fall through：計画・契約などが成立せず、実現しない。
en: awry describes a plan or situation departing from its intended course and developing unsuccessfully.
wrong is the most general word for an error, malfunction, or result contrary to expectation.
amiss suggests that something is not as it should be, sometimes without an identified cause.
off track means diverted from the intended direction of a plan, discussion, or process.
askew primarily describes a physical object positioned unevenly or at an angle.
crooked means physically bent rather than straight or, figuratively, dishonest.
backfire means producing a harmful result opposite to the one intended.
fall through means that a plan, agreement, or arrangement fails to be completed.

etymology.ja: awry は、状態・位置を表す古い前置詞的要素 a-「～の状態で」と wry「ねじれた、曲がった」から成る。wry は「曲げる、向きを変える」という意味を持つ古い英語・ゲルマン語系の語に関係する。もとは顔・視線・物体などが横や斜めにねじれた状態を表した。そこから、物事が正しい方向・予定された経路から「曲がって外れる」という比喩が生じ、計画や状況が失敗するという現代の主要な意味へ発達した。
etymology.en: Awry consists of the old prepositional element a-, meaning in a particular state or position, and wry, meaning twisted or turned. Wry is related to older Germanic words expressing turning or bending. Awry originally described a face, glance, or object turned sideways or crooked. This physical image developed into the figurative idea of events bending away from the proper direction or intended course, producing the modern sense of a plan or situation going wrong.

note.ja: 物事が正しく機能・進行せず、問題や誤りが生じたことを表す一般語。
note.en: The general term for a process, function, or situation becoming erroneous or problematic.

note.ja: 状況に何か問題があり、正常な状態ではないことを表す。
note.en: Indicates that something about a situation is faulty or not as it should be.

note.ja: 本来進むべき方向・経路から外れたことを表す。
note.en: Describes movement or development away from the intended direction or route.

note.ja: 物が正しい位置からずれ、斜めになっていることを主に表す。
note.en: Primarily describes an object that is tilted or displaced from its proper position.

note.ja: 試みが望んだ結果を達成できなかったことを直接表す。
note.en: Directly indicates that an attempt failed to achieve its intended result.

plans go awry

ja: Our travel plans went awry when the last flight was canceled. — 最終便が欠航になり、私たちの旅行計画は狂ってしまった。
If anything goes awry, call me immediately. — 万一何か問題が起きたら、すぐに電話してください。
The event was carefully organized, but several things still went awry. — その催しは入念に準備されていたが、それでもいくつかの問題が生じた。
The filing procedure went awry because the attached document was in an unsupported format. — 添付書類が非対応の形式だったため、出願手続きがうまくいかなかった。
A single mistranslated limitation can cause an otherwise sound patent strategy to go awry. — 一つの限定事項の誤訳によって、それ以外は堅実な特許戦略が狂うこともある。
en: Our travel plans went awry when the last flight was canceled.
If anything goes awry, call me immediately.
The event was carefully organized, but several things still went awry.
The filing procedure went awry because the attached document was in an unsupported format.
A single mistranslated limitation can cause an otherwise sound patent strategy to go awry.

usage.article: The usual idiom is a fool’s errand, not the fool’s errand, unless a previously identified errand is meant.
usage.possessive: Fool’s requires an apostrophe before s because it historically means an errand suitable for or assigned to a fool.
usage.go_and_be: Go on emphasizes undertaking the mission, while be on describes currently pursuing it.
usage.causative: Send someone on a fool’s errand means cause or trick the person into performing a pointless task.
usage.register: Common in critical or humorous commentary but unsuitable for neutral descriptions of another person’s work when politeness is required.

ipa.us: /ˌɡoʊ ɑːn ə ˌfuːlz ˈerənd/; /ˌbiː ɑːn ə ˌfuːlz ˈerənd/
ipa.uk: /ˌɡəʊ ɒn ə ˌfuːlz ˈerənd/; /ˌbiː ɒn ə ˌfuːlz ˈerənd/

ja: 達成できる見込みのない、無益な任務に出かける
時間や労力を費やしても成果が得られない仕事に取り組んでいる
存在しない物や得られない答えを探し求める
人をだましたり、からかったりして、無意味な用事に行かせる
en: to undertake a mission that has little or no chance of success
to be engaged in a task that wastes time and effort without producing a useful result
to search for something that does not exist or an answer that cannot be obtained
to deceive or tease someone by sending them to perform a pointless task

nuance.ja: a fool’s errand は、その仕事が難しいというだけでなく、目的そのものが達成不能・無意味・誤った前提に基づいていることを示唆する。He is on a fool’s errand. は、その人の判断を「愚か」と評価する強い表現になり得るため、対人場面では注意が必要である。send someone on a fool’s errand は、経験の浅い人に存在しない道具を取りに行かせるようないたずらにも、組織が人に無益な仕事を課す場合にも使える。go on は任務への着手、be on はその最中の状態に焦点を置く。非常に困難でも成功の可能性がある仕事には、必ずしも適さない。
nuance.en: A fool’s errand suggests more than an ordinary difficult task: its objective is impossible, pointless, or founded on a mistaken premise. He is on a fool’s errand can strongly criticize the person’s judgment and therefore requires care in interpersonal settings. Send someone on a fool’s errand can describe a practical joke, such as making an inexperienced person search for a nonexistent tool, or an organization assigning someone a futile task. Go on focuses on undertaking the mission, while be on describes being engaged in it. The idiom is not necessarily appropriate for a task that is merely very difficult but still has a realistic chance of success.

ja: a fool’s errand：達成不能または無意味で、労力の無駄となる任務・用事。
a wild-goose chase：存在しない物・見つかりそうにない物を探し回る無駄な追跡。
a futile exercise：望む結果を生まないと分かっている無益な試み。
a lost cause：成功・回復の可能性がほとんどない人・運動・計画。
a waste of time：時間を使う価値のない活動。
an uphill battle：達成は可能かもしれないが、非常に困難な取り組み。
a long shot：成功の可能性は低いものの、完全に不可能とは限らない試み。
mission impossible：達成が極めて困難または不可能に見える任務を表す口語表現。
en: a fool’s errand is an impossible or pointless mission that wastes effort.
a wild-goose chase is a futile search for something nonexistent or extremely unlikely to be found.
a futile exercise is an attempt known to be incapable of producing the desired result.
a lost cause is a person, movement, or plan with almost no possibility of success or recovery.
a waste of time is an activity not worth the time spent on it.
an uphill battle is an extremely difficult undertaking that may still be achievable.
a long shot has a low chance of success but is not necessarily impossible.
mission impossible is an informal description of a task that appears extremely difficult or impossible.

etymology.ja: errand は古英語 ǣrende「伝言、任務、用事」に由来する。fool’s errand は文字どおりには「愚か者の用事」であり、成果が得られない任務や、だまされた人だけが引き受けるような用事を表すようになった。この表現は、初心者やだまされやすい人を、存在しない物を取りに行かせるという古くからのいたずらとも結び付いている。ただし、特定の一つの物語や慣習だけから生まれたと断定できる表現ではない。
etymology.en: Errand comes from Old English aerende, meaning a message, mission, or piece of business. A fool’s errand literally suggests an errand suitable for a fool and developed into a term for a mission that cannot produce a useful result or that only a deceived person would undertake. The expression is also associated with the long-standing practical joke of sending an inexperienced or gullible person to fetch a nonexistent object. It cannot, however, be securely attributed to one particular story or custom.

note.ja: 見つからない物・人・答えを求めて、無駄に探し回ることに重点がある。
note.en: Emphasizes a futile pursuit or search for an object, person, or answer that cannot be found.

note.ja: 最初から有益な結果を生まない試みであることを表す、比較的形式的な表現。
note.en: A relatively formal expression for an undertaking incapable of producing a useful result.

note.ja: 成功・改善・救済の見込みがほとんど失われた対象を表す。
note.en: A person, objective, or undertaking for which hope of success, improvement, or rescue is nearly gone.

note.ja: 努力しても成果・結果が得られない仕事。
note.en: A task that produces no useful result despite the effort invested.

note.ja: 費やした労力に見合う成果が期待できないことを直接表す。
note.en: A direct expression for activity unlikely to produce a result worth the effort expended.

ja: We went on a fool’s errand looking for a shop that had closed years ago. — 私たちは、何年も前に閉店した店を探すという無駄足を踏んだ。
Trying to satisfy everyone may be a fool’s errand. — 全員を満足させようとするのは、無益な試みかもしれない。
The senior workers sent the new employee on a fool’s errand to find a nonexistent tool. — 先輩社員たちは、存在しない道具を探させる無意味なお使いに新人を行かせた。
Searching for a patent without first defining the relevant technical features can become a fool’s errand. — 関連する技術的特徴を最初に定義せずに特許を探すことは、無益な作業になり得る。
The attorney warned that pursuing damages against an insolvent company might be a costly fool’s errand. — 弁護士は、支払能力のない会社に損害賠償を求めても、費用のかかる徒労に終わる可能性があると警告した。

Trying to satisfy everyone may be a fool’s errand.

Searching for a patent without first defining the relevant technical features can become a fool’s errand.
The attorney warned that pursuing damages against an insolvent company might be a costly fool’s errand.

usage.movement: An errand normally involves going somewhere to perform a relatively small practical task.
usage.verb: Run is the most characteristic verb: run an errand or run errands.
usage.purpose: The purpose may be introduced by to plus a verb: an errand to collect a parcel.
usage.beneficiary: For identifies the person whose business is being done: I ran an errand for my neighbor.
usage.plural: Run errands commonly describes completing several routine tasks in one outing.
usage.person_terms: Errand boy and errand girl can sound dated or demeaning when applied to an adult employee.

ja: 物を買う・届ける・受け取るために出かけて済ませる用事
人から頼まれて行う短い外出を伴う仕事
日常生活で行う買い物・銀行・郵便などの細かな用事
物・書類・伝言などを特定の場所や人へ運ぶ任務
en: a short trip made to buy, deliver, or collect something
a small practical task involving travel that is performed for another person
a routine personal task such as shopping or visiting a bank or post office
a mission to carry an object, document, or message to a particular person or place

nuance.ja: errand は単なる task ではなく、通常、用事を果たすために自宅・職場などからどこかへ移動することを含む。郵便局で荷物を出す、薬局で薬を受け取る、銀行に寄るといった比較的小さく実務的な用事が典型である。run errands は走ることを意味せず、複数の用事を次々に済ませることを表す。仕事で重要書類を官庁へ届ける場合も errand と呼べるが、専門的・重要な任務には assignment、mission、filing などの方が適切なこともある。I have an errand to run. は、用事の内容を詳しく説明せず一時的にその場を離れる際にも使われる。
nuance.en: An errand differs from a general task because it normally involves going somewhere away from one’s home or workplace. Typical errands include mailing a parcel, collecting medicine, visiting a bank, or buying groceries. Run errands does not imply literal running; it means completing one or more such practical tasks. Delivering an important document to an authority can also be described as an errand, although assignment, mission, or filing may be more suitable when emphasizing professional importance. I have an errand to run can explain a temporary departure without specifying the details.

ja: errand：小さな実務的用事を済ませるための外出。
task：行う必要がある仕事・作業全般。外出を伴うとは限らない。
chore：日常的に繰り返す家事・雑務。面倒な仕事という含みを持つことがある。
assignment：職場・学校などで正式に割り当てられた仕事・課題。
mission：特定の重要な目的を達成するための任務。
delivery：物・荷物・書類などを目的地へ届ける行為。
favor：他人を助けるために行う親切な行為。
appointment：医師・顧客などと、特定の時刻に会う約束。
en: an errand is a short trip made to complete a small practical task.
a task is any piece of work that needs to be done and does not necessarily involve travel.
a chore is a routine household or minor job and may suggest something tedious.
an assignment is a task formally given in employment or education.
a mission is a task undertaken to achieve a particular and often important objective.
a delivery is the act of taking an object, parcel, or document to its destination.
a favor is an act of kindness performed to help another person.
an appointment is an arrangement to meet someone at a specified time.

etymology.ja: 古英語 ǣrende「伝言、任務、用事」に由来し、古いゲルマン諸語の同族語と関係する。もともとは、人に伝えるべき知らせや、特定の目的をもって遂行する任務を表した。使者が伝言や依頼を果たすために出かけるという関係から、物を届ける・受け取る・購入するといった短い外出を伴う日常的な用事を意味するようになった。直前の fool’s errand は、この errand に fool’s が付き、「愚か者にふさわしい無益な任務」を表す。
etymology.en: Errand comes from Old English aerende, meaning a message, mission, or piece of business, and is related to cognates in other early Germanic languages. It originally referred to information that had to be conveyed or a mission undertaken for a particular purpose. Because a messenger traveled to deliver the message or complete the business, the word developed its modern sense of a short trip to deliver, collect, or purchase something. In fool’s errand, the same noun is modified by fool’s to describe a pointless mission.

note.ja: 完了する必要のある仕事・作業を広く表し、移動の有無を問わない。
note.en: A broad term for work that must be completed, whether or not travel is involved.

note.ja: 掃除・洗濯など、日常的に繰り返す小さな仕事・家事。
note.en: A small routine job, especially household work such as cleaning or washing.

note.ja: 雇用主・教師などによって正式に与えられた仕事・課題。
note.en: A task formally allocated by an employer, teacher, or other authority.

note.ja: 明確で、しばしば重要な目的を達成するために遂行される任務。
note.en: An undertaking carried out to achieve a clear and often important objective.

note.ja: 完了する必要のある特定の仕事を表す一般的な語。
note.en: A general word for a particular piece of work that needs to be completed.

usage.uncountable: Courtesy without an article commonly means polite and considerate behavior.
usage.countable: A courtesy is a particular considerate act, privilege, or conventional gesture.
usage.attributive: Before a noun, courtesy can indicate something provided free of charge or performed as a polite gesture.
usage.courtesy_of: Courtesy of identifies the person or organization providing something and can also indicate the source of an image or material.
usage.sarcasm: Courtesy of may be used ironically to identify the unwelcome cause of a problem.

ja: 他人への敬意・配慮を示す礼儀正しい態度
相手への思いやりから行う個別の親切・便宜

an individual act of kindness, consideration, or accommodation
an action conventionally expected as a matter of social or professional politeness
attributively, a service or facility provided without charge
in courtesy of, through the kindness, provision, or sponsorship of a person or organization
a formula identifying the source that supplied an image, item, or information

nuance.ja: courtesy は、単なる作法の知識ではなく、相手を尊重し負担を減らそうとする態度や行為を表す。He had the courtesy to call. は「彼には電話をする程度の礼儀はあった」という意味で、文脈によっては非難を含む。as a courtesy は、法的義務ではなく配慮として行うことを示す場合があるが、この表現だけで法的義務の有無が決まるわけではない。courtesy copy は正式な送達・提出とは別に参考として送る写し、courtesy bus は顧客向けの無料送迎車である。courtesy of the storm のような皮肉な用法では、「嵐のおかげで」という好ましくない原因を示す。
nuance.en: Courtesy concerns not merely knowledge of etiquette but conduct intended to respect others and reduce inconvenience. He had the courtesy to call means that he showed at least the expected consideration by calling and may carry an implied criticism. As a courtesy can indicate that an act is voluntary rather than legally required, but the phrase itself does not determine whether a legal obligation exists. A courtesy copy is supplied for information separately from formal service or filing, while a courtesy bus is free transportation for customers. In an ironic expression such as courtesy of the storm, courtesy of identifies an unwelcome cause.

ja: courtesy：相手への敬意・配慮を示す礼儀正しさ、または個別の親切。
politeness：失礼にならない言葉遣い・態度を広く表す。
civility：対立があっても保たれる、最低限の礼節ある振る舞い。
etiquette：特定の社会・職業・場面で守るべき作法・慣例。
manners：人が社会生活で示す行儀・振る舞い。
kindness：人を助けたい、苦痛を減らしたいという親切心と行為。
favor：人のために行う個別の親切・便宜。
complimentary：商品・サービスが無料で提供されることを明確に表す。
en: courtesy is respectful consideration for others or a particular considerate act.
politeness broadly describes language and behavior that avoid giving offense.
civility is a basic level of respectful conduct maintained even during disagreement.
etiquette is the accepted code of behavior for a particular society, profession, or occasion.
manners are a person’s socially observable standards of behavior.
kindness is the desire and action to help people or reduce their distress.
a favor is an individual helpful act performed for another person.
complimentary explicitly means that a product or service is supplied free of charge.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 curteisie「宮廷風の礼儀、上品な振る舞い」に由来し、court「宮廷」と同じ語族に属する。もとは宮廷にふさわしい洗練された態度や騎士的な作法を表した。そこから身分や場所を問わず、他人への礼儀・配慮・親切を広く意味するようになった。courteous「礼儀正しい」も同じ起源を持つ。courtesy service のような無料提供の意味は、顧客への厚意としてサービスを行うという発想から生じた。
etymology.en: Courtesy comes from Old French curteisie, meaning courtly manners or refined conduct, and belongs to the same word family as court. It originally described behavior considered appropriate at a royal or noble court, including refinement and chivalrous manners. Its meaning broadened to respectful and considerate conduct toward others regardless of rank or setting. Courteous shares the same origin. The free-of-charge sense in expressions such as courtesy service developed from the idea of providing something as a considerate gesture to a customer or guest.

note.ja: 言葉遣い・態度が社会的に適切で、相手に不快感を与えないこと。
note.en: Socially appropriate language or behavior that avoids offending others.

note.ja: 意見の対立がある状況でも相手に示す、節度ある礼儀正しさ。
note.en: Restrained and respectful conduct, particularly when people disagree.

note.ja: 自分の行動が相手の感情・事情・必要性に及ぼす影響への配慮。
note.en: Attention to how one’s conduct affects another person’s feelings, circumstances, or needs.

note.ja: 相手を助けたり苦痛を減らしたりしようとする思いやり。
note.en: Concern expressed through an effort to help another person or reduce their distress.

note.ja: 相手を助けるために行う具体的な親切・便宜。
note.en: A specific helpful act performed for another person.

ja: He had the courtesy to inform us that he would be late. — 彼には、遅れることを私たちに知らせるだけの礼儀はあった。
Please treat every visitor with courtesy and respect. — すべての来訪者に礼儀と敬意をもって接してください。
The hotel provides a courtesy bus to the airport. — そのホテルは空港まで無料送迎バスを運行している。
As a professional courtesy, we sent opposing counsel a copy of the document. — 職業上の礼儀として、私たちは相手方代理人にその書類の写しを送った。
The patent attorney provided a courtesy copy of the response, but warned that it did not constitute formal service. — 弁理士は応答書の参考用写しを提供したが、それは正式な送達には当たらないと注意を促した。
en: He had the courtesy to inform us that he would be late.
Please treat every visitor with courtesy and respect.
The hotel provides a courtesy bus to the airport.
As a professional courtesy, we sent opposing counsel a copy of the document.
The patent attorney provided a courtesy copy of the response, but warned that it did not constitute formal service.

patterns: be courteous in dealing with + person
it was courteous of someone to do

usage.person: Courteous commonly describes a person who behaves with politeness and respect.
usage.behavior: It can also modify conduct or communication: a courteous reply.
usage.preposition: Use to or toward / towards for the person receiving the courtesy.
usage.evaluation: Use of plus a person after an impersonal construction: It was courteous of her to reply.
usage.comparison: More courteous and most courteous are preferred to courteser and courtest.
usage.spelling: The standard spelling is courteous, not courtus; the middle vowel sequence reflects its relationship with courtesy.

ja: 他人に礼儀正しく敬意を示す
相手の感情や事情に配慮した、丁重な
発言・返答・態度などが失礼でなく、節度のある
対立や不満があっても礼節を保っている
en: polite and respectful toward other people
considerate of another person’s feelings or circumstances
for a reply, manner, or action, properly respectful and not offensive
maintaining civility despite disagreement or dissatisfaction

nuance.ja: courteous は、表面的に丁寧な言葉を使うだけでなく、相手を尊重し、その立場や負担に配慮して振る舞うことを表す。polite とほぼ同義だが、courteous の方がやや形式的で、職業上の応対・書面・公的な場面に適している。courteous but firm は、相手への敬意を保ちながらも、要求・期限・反対意見を曖昧にしない姿勢を表す。相手の意見に同意することまでは意味せず、厳しい拒絶や反論も courteous に伝えることができる。
nuance.en: Courteous describes more than the use of polite words; it suggests behavior that respects another person and takes account of their position or convenience. It is close to polite but somewhat more formal and especially natural for professional service, correspondence, and public conduct. Courteous but firm describes maintaining respect while clearly communicating a demand, deadline, or disagreement. Courtesy does not require agreement, so even a strong refusal or objection can be expressed courteously.

ja: courteous：相手への敬意と配慮を示す、やや形式的な「礼儀正しい」。
polite：社会的な作法に従い、失礼でないことを表す最も一般的な語。
civil：対立・不満があっても、最低限の礼節を保っている。
considerate：自分の行動が相手の感情・必要性に及ぼす影響をよく考える。
respectful：相手の地位・権利・感情などに敬意を示す。
gracious：親切で品があり、相手を快適にさせる寛大な態度を示す。
deferential：目上の人や権威ある人に敬意を示して控えめに振る舞う。
courtly：宮廷風に洗練され、儀礼的に丁重な。古風・文学的。
en: courteous means showing respectful consideration and is somewhat more formal than polite.
polite is the most general word for behaving according to accepted manners and avoiding offense.
civil means maintaining a basic level of politeness despite disagreement or hostility.
considerate means thinking carefully about how one’s conduct affects another person’s feelings or needs.
respectful means showing regard for another person’s status, rights, feelings, or dignity.
gracious suggests kind, dignified, and generous behavior that makes others feel comfortable.
deferential means respectfully yielding or showing restraint toward a senior or authoritative person.
courtly means refined and ceremoniously polite in an old-fashioned or literary manner.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 corteis「宮廷風の、礼儀正しい」に由来し、court「宮廷」と同じ語族に属する。もとは宮廷にふさわしい洗練された作法や騎士的な態度を表した。そこから、身分や場所を問わず、人に敬意と配慮を示す「礼儀正しい」という一般的な意味へ広がった。名詞 courtesy も同じ起源を持つ。綴りは courtus ではなく courteous であり、語末の -eous はおおむね /iəs/ と発音される。
etymology.en: Courteous comes from Old French corteis, meaning courtly or polite, and belongs to the same word family as court. It originally described refined manners and chivalrous conduct considered appropriate at a royal or noble court. Its meaning broadened to respectful and considerate behavior toward others in any social setting. The noun courtesy shares the same origin. The standard spelling is courteous rather than courtus, and the final sequence is pronounced approximately /iəs/.

note.ja: 一般に認められた作法に従い、相手に失礼のないよう振る舞う。
note.en: Behaving according to accepted manners and avoiding offense.

note.ja: 親しみや好意がなくても、対立相手に最低限の礼儀を示す。
note.en: Maintaining a minimum level of politeness even without friendliness or agreement.

note.ja: 相手の感情・負担・都合を考えて行動する。
note.en: Taking account of another person’s feelings, burden, or convenience.

note.ja: 人の尊厳・地位・意見などを尊重する態度を示す。
note.en: Showing regard for another person’s dignity, position, or views.

note.ja: 礼儀正しさに加え、温かさ・品格・寛大さを感じさせる。
note.en: Showing warmth, dignity, and generosity in addition to politeness.

ja: The receptionist was courteous and helpful throughout our visit. — 受付係は、私たちの滞在中ずっと礼儀正しく親切だった。
It was courteous of her to inform us about the delay in advance. — 遅延について事前に知らせてくれたのは、彼女の丁重な配慮だった。
Even when the discussion became heated, he remained courteous. — 議論が白熱しても、彼は礼儀正しい態度を崩さなかった。
Our reply should be courteous but firm about the payment deadline. — 私たちの返答は丁重でありながら、支払期限については毅然としたものであるべきだ。
The patent attorney sent a courteous response explaining why the proposed amendment could not be accepted. — 弁理士は、提案された補正を受け入れられない理由を説明する丁重な返答を送った。

Even when the discussion became heated, he remained courteous.
